To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) there is a significant relationship between the frequency of the occurrence of intrafamiliar violence and the low academic performance; (b) there is a negative correlation between the low academic performance and the frequency of the intrafamiliar violence; and (c) the low academic performance of students is a consequence of the intrafamilial violence.
violence in the family is the cause of low performance in school, and that this violence is caused by the aggressors who are parents, which affects young girls between 12 and 15 years old.
the students who have experienced violence in their families have a low academic performance, a low self-esteem and a low development of the personality.

the effects of domestic violence on the academic performance of students aged 12-15.
the relationship between violence against women and children in their families and the effects on their school achievement.
the effects of intrafamiliar violence on academic performance of students aged between 12 and 15, in the city of San Cristobal, Venezuela.
